1  THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR HEARING ON 07.10.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.519/2018 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kozhikode,
(the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 30/09/2019.
The sole respondent herein is the third respondent/insurer in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 22/10/2017 at about 10:00 p.m., while he was pillion riding on motorcycle bearing registration no.KL-65/D-9411 ridden by the second respondent along beach road in Kozhikode, and when he reached Nainamvalappu road, due to the rash and negligent riding of the latter, the motorcycle collided with motorcycle bearing 2025:KER:74051 registration no.KL-11/AP-9648, as a result of which the claim petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
A sum of 4,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The first respondent/owner and the second respondent/rider of the offending motorcycle filed written statement denying negligence on the part of latter.
The compensation claimed under various heads was contended to be exorbitant.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy but denying liability.
The averments in the petition regarding age, occupation and income and injuries sustained to the claim petitioner were disputed.
Compensation claimed under various heads was contended to be excessive.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A1
to A5 and Ext.X1 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No documentary evidence was produced by the third respondent/insurer.

sentences.text: The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the second respondent/rider of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 3,03,300/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.

Aggrieved by the Award,
the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides.
9. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner-
Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter a salesman, was earning 20,000/- per month.

However, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at 2025:KER:74051 7,000/-, which is quite low going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236.
9.1.

entities.text:
Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the light of the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra), the notional income is fixed as 11,000/-.
Loss of earnings 10.

The materials on record show that the claim petitioner sustained the following injuries- " Fracture shaft of the left femur, both bone fracture left leg, lacerated wound over left thigh, 3rd and 4th toe and abrasions over left wrist left arm, right elbow, 2nd to 5th fingers,"
He was hospitalised for a period of 5 days.
In all probability he might have been unable to work for a period of five months.

Hence, he can be awarded compensation for a period of five months, that is,
11,000/- x 5 = 55,000/-.
Pain and suffering 11.
In the light of the injuries sustained and the period of hospitalisation, an amount of 50,000/- as claimed under this head can be awarded as it is just and reasonable.
2025: KER:74051 Loss of amenities 12.
An amount of 50,000/- was claimed.
The Tribunal awarded amount rupees 30,000/-.
In the facts and circumstances case, 50,000/- as claimed appears to be just and reasonable.
Extra nourishment 13.
The accident took place on 22/10/2017.
Hence, compensation at the rate of 450/- per day for a period of 5 days can be granted, that is, 2,250/- .

14. The impugned Award is modified to the following extent:

The third respondent/
insurer is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On deposit of the amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to 2025:KER:74051 the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
